title: Claude Opus 4.5
hook: Anthropic's Opus 4.5 pushed frontier coding and agentic tool use forward — and cut Opus pricing sharply, making the top tier far cheaper to run at scale.
key_points: Released November 2025, positioned as a leading model for coding, agents, and computer use.
A major price reduction over earlier Opus models, lowering the cost of frontier-tier work.
Part of the rapid Claude 4.x cadence between Claude 4 (May 2025) and later 4.x releases.
Aimed at long-horizon agentic tasks that chain many tool calls together.
content_html: Anthropic released Claude Opus 4.5 in November 2025, advancing its most capable tier with a focus on coding, agentic tool use, and computer use. Alongside the capability gains, Anthropic cut Opus pricing substantially — a notable move, since the Opus line had historically carried a steep premium.
extra_html:
What's new

Opus 4.5 continued the fast Claude 4.x cadence, slotting between the original Claude 4 of May 2025 and the later 4.x models. The emphasis was on real-world agentic performance: sustaining long chains of reasoning and tool calls reliably, the kind of workload that powers coding agents and computer-use automation. The price reduction made running the top model at scale far more practical for production deployments.

Why it matters

The combination of a capability bump and a large price cut reflected the competitive dynamic of late 2025: frontier quality was becoming cheaper fast, driven by efficiency gains and pressure from strong open-weight models. For builders, a cheaper Opus changed the calculus of when to reach for the most capable model versus a smaller one. See Anthropic's announcement for specifics.

related.hook: Claude 4 lets a model interleave reasoning with tool calls - thinking, calling a tool, thinking again, and even running tools in parallel - rather than reasoning once and answering.

related.hook: Claude Opus 4.7's gains land hardest on the hardest software-engineering tasks, and it now checks its own work - better self-verification of its outputs alongside the coding boost.

related.hook: What if a model could critique and improve its own answers against a written set of principles, instead of relying on humans to label every harmful case?
